title: Sunny and the Silver Dew | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka discovers that overnight a spider has woven a web between two grass stalks, and now the morning dew has turned it into a necklace of tiny silver beads glittering in the last of the moonlight. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The web caught the light.

Sunny almost walked into it — her paw was already raised — when she saw it, stretched between two grass stalks at exactly the height of her nose. A perfect spiral of silk, strung with dew.

Every single thread had dew on it. Tiny round drops, spaced perfectly, each one a sphere of water so small she had to look hard to believe it was there. And each one — each tiny sphere — held a reflection of the moon inside it.

A hundred tiny moons.

She stepped back very carefully so as not to disturb it.

The web was enormous for a spider — as wide across as both her paws spread flat. She looked for the spider and found it at the edge, motionless, waiting.

Patient. Still. Everything in order.

Sunny crouched down to look at the web at eye level.

At this angle the dew drops caught the moonlight differently. They weren't just drops — they were tiny lanterns. Tiny lit windows, each one containing something glowing and silver and round.

She breathed very slowly so as not to make a breeze.

The web held its hundred moons.

She sat down in the grass beside it and watched until her eyes grew heavy.

All those perfect small things, quietly glowing.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, silver dew. Goodnight, little one.
